title: Continuous boundary lifts for a Kan fibration admit simplicial lifts
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and geometric realization of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $p:E\to T$ be a simplicial map lifting every horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq m$ (a Kan fibration). For $n\geq0$, let $\partial\Delta^n$ be the union of the proper faces, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Let $a:\partial\Delta^n\to E$ and $b:\Delta^n\to T$ be simplicial maps satisfying $pa=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$. Suppose a continuous map $h:|\Delta^n|\to|E|$ satisfies $|p|h=|b|$ and $h|_{|\partial\Delta^n|}=|a|$, where restriction uses the realized boundary inclusion. Then there is a simplicial map $c:\Delta^n\to E$ with $pc=b$ and $c|_{\partial\Delta^n}=a$. No Kan assumption on $E$ or $T$, weak-equivalence hypothesis on $p$, or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated relative boundary-lifting comparison, a corollary of Theorem 3.5.9 (minimal-fibration retract factorization), Corollary 3.5.7 (local triviality over a simplex), Lemmas 3.4.5–3.4.6 and the proof of Proposition 3.4.7 (nullhomotopy, horn contraction, and prescribed-boundary prism extension; prism lifting from Theorems 3.3.1–3.3.2), and Proposition 3.6.3 (simplicial/realized homotopy-group comparison). This precise relative formulation is not a quoted numbered theorem. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-minimal-factorization] to p. We obtain a simplicial subset E' of E, maps s:E'\to E and r:E\to E' with rs=1, and q=ps:E'\to T such that p=qr; r has the right lifting property against every boundary inclusion, and for the given simplex b:\Delta^n\to T there are a Kan complex F_b and an isomorphism \theta:\Delta^n\times_T E'\cong\Delta^n\times F_b over \Delta^n. The factorization theorem imposes no Kan condition on E or T, so it applies under exactly the hypotheses here.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.9 and Corollary 3.5.7 (minimal-fibration retract and simplexwise product)

proof.text: Form the degreewise pullback E'_b=\Delta^n\times_T E'. The composite r\circ a: \partial\Delta^n\to E' and the continuous map |r|\circ h:|\Delta^n|\to|E'| both lie over |b|, and the latter restricts to |r\circ a| on |\partial\Delta^n|. By preservation of finite limits and products under realization in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], the isomorphism \theta realizes to a homeomorphism in the category of k-spaces |E'_b|\cong|\Delta^n|\times|F_b| over |\Delta^n|. The map $(1,|r|h)$ into the realized pullback is continuous by its k-space universal property, since $|\Delta^n|$ is a k-space. Hence it determines a continuous map H:|\Delta^n|\to|F_b| whose boundary is the realization of the simplicial map \alpha:\partial\Delta^n\to F_b obtained from r\circ a and \theta.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.9, Corollary 3.5.7 and the realization finite-limit comparison

proof.text: Put $K=F_b$. First record explicitly how to extend a prescribed simplicial homotopy. For a degreewise inclusion $C\hookrightarrow L$, apply [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map] to $K\to\Delta^0$: restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(L,K)\to\operatorname{Fun}(C,K)$ is a Kan fibration. A homotopy $C\times\Delta^1\to K$ is an edge below this fibration. Given an extension to $L$ at either endpoint, lift that edge using the corresponding one-dimensional horn $\{0\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ or $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$; evaluation at the other endpoint extends its boundary map. In particular, for $C=\partial\Delta^n$ and $L=\Delta^n$, extendability is invariant under each simplicial boundary homotopy in either orientation, hence under any finite zigzag of such homotopies. This does not reverse the simplicial interval.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.1; the first paragraph of the proof of Proposition 3.4.7, with the endpoint lift specified

proof.text: For $n=0$, the continuous map $H$ supplies a point of $|K|$. By the realization quotient definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], such a point has a representative in a simplex of $K$; any vertex of that simplex supplies $d_F:\Delta^0\to K$. Thus an empty $K$ is impossible here. For $n=1$, $H$ is a path between the two vertices of $\alpha$. The component bijection of [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre] puts them in one simplicial component, so there is a finite edge zigzag between them. Reverse a backward edge by filling the outer $2$-horn whose known edges are that edge and the degenerate edge at its source; the third edge has the reverse endpoints. Compose two successive forward edges by filling their inner $2$-horn. Iterating gives one edge $d_F$ with exactly the prescribed endpoints; for a length-zero zigzag take the degenerate edge. These settle both low dimensions.

source.place: Definition 3.4.1, Lemmas 3.4.2–3.4.3; the dimension-zero case of the relative comparison

proof.text: Assume $n\geq2$, set $A=\Lambda_n^n\subseteq\partial\Delta^n$, and let $x=\alpha(n)$. The order-preserving map $[n]\times[1]\to[n]$ taking $(v,0)$ to $v$ and $(v,1)$ to $n$ induces a simplicial contraction $C:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^n$. It preserves $A$: a simplex of $A$ omits a vertex $i<n$, and the contraction adds only the vertex $n$. Its restriction fixes $n$. Hence $\alpha C|_{A\times\Delta^1}$ contracts $\alpha|_A$ to $x$. Apply the restriction fibration in step 3 with $C=A$, $L=\partial\Delta^n$, and prescribed endpoint $\alpha$, to obtain $G:\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to K$ agreeing with this contraction on $A$ and with $\alpha$ at time zero. Write $g=G_1$. Then $g|_A=x$, and $\sigma=g d_n:\Delta^{n-1}\to K$ is constant at $x$ on its boundary, since every proper face of $d_n\Delta^{n-1}$ lies in $A$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.6 and the horn-contraction paragraph in the proof of Proposition 3.4.7

proof.text: The map $g$ still has a continuous extension $J:|\Delta^n|\to|K|$, as the following formula verifies. Use the disk/boundary homeomorphism and product-realization comparison of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] to view $H$ as $H_D:D^n\to|K|$ and $|G|$ as $G_D:S^{n-1}\times[0,1]\to|K|$, with $G_D(z,0)=H_D(z)$. On the disk define $J_D(u)=H_D(2u)$ for $\|u\|\leq1/2$, and $J_D(u)=G_D(u/\|u\|,2\|u\|-1)$ for $\|u\|\geq1/2$. The formulas agree at $\|u\|=1/2$, so pasting makes $J_D$ continuous, and its boundary is $g$. Translate back to $J$ on the simplex. The formula $N(z,t)=J((1-t)d_n(z)+t e_n)$, where $z\in|\Delta^{n-1}|$ and $e_n$ is the last vertex, is a nullhomotopy of $|\sigma|$. For $z$ in the boundary, the entire segment to $e_n$ lies in $|A|$ and $J|_{|A|}=x$; thus $N$ fixes the whole boundary and is a based nullhomotopy.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.4.7 and Proposition 3.6.3; explicit topological collar and based-nullhomotopy calculation supplied by the agent

proof.text: By injectivity of the realization isomorphism $\pi_{n-1}^s(K,x)\cong\pi_{n-1}(|K|,x)$ in [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre], step 6 implies $[\sigma]=0$. By the definition of $\pi_{n-1}^s$ in that cited statement, this equality is witnessed by a finite zigzag of based simplicial homotopies from $\sigma$ to the constant $(n-1)$-simplex at $x$. Extend each homotopy to $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ by making it constant at $x$ on $A\times\Delta^1$ and using the given based homotopy on $d_n\Delta^{n-1}\times\Delta^1$. These prescriptions agree on the intersection $\partial(d_n\Delta^{n-1})\times\Delta^1$, so they glue degreewise. They give a boundary-homotopy zigzag from $g$ to the constant boundary map. The latter extends by the constant $n$-simplex. Apply the endpoint-lifting argument of step 3 successively along this zigzag, starting at that constant filler, to extend $g$. Finally apply it to $G$ from step 5, with the known extension at time one, to obtain $d_F:\Delta^n\to K$ whose boundary is exactly $\alpha$. Thus all dimensions are covered.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.3 and the homotopy-extension argument in the proof of Proposition 3.4.7; the zigzag and all boundary prescriptions are explicit

proof.text: Define $c'=\operatorname{pr}_{E'}\theta^{-1}(1_{\Delta^n},d_F):\Delta^n\to E'$. Since $\theta$ is over $\Delta^n$, $qc'=b$. On $\partial\Delta^n$, the pair $(1,d_F)$ restricts to $(1,\alpha)$, which by the definition of $\alpha$ in step 2 is $\theta(1,r a)$. Applying $\theta^{-1}$ and the projection gives $c'|_{\partial\Delta^n}=r a$.

source.place: Corollary 3.5.7; explicit projection and boundary calculation

proof.text: Apply the boundary lifting property of $r:E\to E'$ from [lem-coef-kan-minimal-factorization] to the square with left map $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, right map $r$, top map $a$, and bottom map $c'$. Step 8 gives its commutativity. The lift $c:\Delta^n\to E$ satisfies $rc=c'$ and $c|_{\partial\Delta^n}=a$, also for $n=0$ because the lifting statement includes the empty boundary. Finally $pc=qrc=qc'=b$.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.9; final boundary lift through the retraction

lean.statement: theorem exists_lift_of_realization_boundary_lift {E T : SSet.{u}} (p : E ⟶ T) (hp : ∀ (m : ℕ) (i : Fin (m + 2)), HasLiftingProperty (horn (m + 1) i).ι p) (n : ℕ) (a : (boundary n).toSSet ⟶ E) (b : (Δ[n] : SSet.{u}) ⟶ T) (hab : a ≫ p = (boundary n).ι ≫ b) (h : (toTop.obj (Δ[n] : SSet.{u})) → toTop.obj E) (hh : Continuous h) (hbase : (toTop.map p).hom ∘ h = (toTop.map b).hom) (hboundary : h ∘ (toTop.map (boundary n).ι).hom = (toTop.map a).hom) : ∃ c : (Δ[n] : SSet.{u}) ⟶ E, c ≫ p = b ∧ (boundary n).ι ≫ c = a
